text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS

-- National Assembly to give second reading to bill on introducing pension funds to France. Labour union leaders warn against threat it implies for existing universal retirement schemes, since employer contributions to pension funds would benefit from social security contribution exemptions.
-- Government launches reform of SNCF state-owned railroad, which plans to separate operations from infrastructure ownership and maintenance.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Paris bourse blue-chip CAC-40 index reached historic high on Monday.
-- Talks between Credit Lyonnais executives and government on restructuring plans for the state-owned bank to end in about two weeks.
-- Axa executives to fill the major posts at the new Axa-UAP insurance group in France.
L'AGEFI
-- Cac-40 index hits record 2,361.27 points due to a favourable international context.
-- Government considers cutting interest rate on housing savings schemes, set at 5.25 percent since 1994.
-- Lazard Freres tops for seventh consecutive year a magazine ranking on mergers and acquisitions activity, after closing 45 deals for a total value of 168.2 billion francs.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Bourse experts remain confident on upward trend, do not see equity as overvalued.
-- Credit Lyonnais chairman confirms to EU Commission that the sale of the bank's European network would generate a 9-billion-franc loss.
-- National Assembly Finance Committee speaker Philippe Auberger says tax reform should protect productive savings, reaffirms opposition to re-introducing ceilings on wealth tax.

-- Compagnie des Signaux chairman Yazid Sabeg says Matra is the only candidate with the financial means of buying Thomson-CSF without running into excess indebtedness and without seeking international alliances.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Early retirement at 55 proves popular, but most politicians reject it.
